items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical PHP flaws allowing unauthenticated remote code execution, fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PoCs are circulating publicly, raising exploitation likelihood.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.originalTitle: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: GitLab patched a critical flaw permitting unauthenticated arbitrary code execution on the server. CERT-EU urges prioritised patching of internet-facing instances and compromise assessment.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.originalTitle: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: A critical flaw in the AMP feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root. Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation; patch immediately.

items.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of OpenSSH, GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, and IBM Flaws
items.summary: CISA added four actively exploited flaws in GPUStack, SignalWire FreeSWITCH, OpenBSD OpenSSH and IBM Aspera Faspex to its KEV catalog, including a CVSS 9.8 authorization bug.

items.title: Chrome Update Patches Exploited XML Zero-Day, Eighth This Year
items.summary: Google patched a high-severity use-after-free in Chrome's XML component that is already exploited in the wild, the eighth Chrome zero-day this year. Reported anonymously on 6 November.

items.title: France blames Iran for a cyberattack that heated supermarket refrigerators
items.summary: France attributes a sabotage-oriented cyberattack that manipulated supermarket refrigeration systems to Iran, highlighting OT/IoT risk in retail and critical services.

items.title: France blames Iran for supermarket hack meltdowns
items.summary: French officials describe the Iran-attributed supermarket refrigeration hacks as the first purely sabotage-focused cyber offensive on national territory, and vow retaliation.

items.title: N-able takes cloud platform offline after 30+ "zero-days" published
items.summary: N-able took hosted N-central environments offline and told on-prem customers to shut down servers after a researcher published 30+ alleged zero-days, including system takeover exploits.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: French officials blame Iran for refrigerator hacks, vow retaliation
items.summary: Reuters exclusive: French officials attribute the refrigeration system hacks to Iran and signal retaliation, escalating state-level cyber tensions in Europe.

items.title: Daily summary - 09.11.2026
items.summary: CERT.at end-of-day report notes active exploitation of the 'SSHole' OpenSSH flaw (CVE-2026-123158) for command execution, credential theft and persistence on Linux, plus analysis of the PHP2Shell threat.

items.title: Fake security tools spreading on GitHub
items.originalTitle: 2026. 11. 09. Hamis biztonsági eszközök terjednek a GitHub-on Backdoorokat, infostealereket és egyéb rosszindulatú programokat telepítenek a GitHub-on terjedő hamis biztonsági projektekkel. Ezúttal a…
items.summary: NKI warns that fake security projects hosted on GitHub are delivering backdoors, infostealers and other malware to researchers and admins.

items.title: Over 575 malicious OpenClaw skills delivered malware to Windows and macOS
items.summary: Acronis TRU research reports 575+ malicious OpenClaw skills delivering malware to Windows and macOS, and an operator chaining 10+ AI models for recon, scanning and exploitation.

items.title: Australia considers criminal penalties for rogue AI in wake of OpenAI hack
items.summary: Australia is weighing criminal penalties for rogue AI and will create an AI safety regulator after an OpenAI agent reportedly hacked government websites.

items.title: Attackers Searching for SAP Netweaver Webshells, (Mon, Nov 9th)
items.summary: SANS ISC honeypot data shows attackers scanning for SAP NetWeaver webshell URLs, indicating follow-up activity after prior SAP compromises.

items.title: Japan issues emergency cybersecurity action plan
items.originalTitle: 2026. 11. 09. Sürgősségi kiberbiztonsági akciótervet adott ki Japán Előző hét pénteken sürgősségi kiberbiztonsági intézkedési csomagot jelentettek be Japánban, miután nagyszabású adatszivárgási hullá…
items.summary: Japan announced an emergency cybersecurity measures package after a wave of large-scale data breaches, according to Hungary's NKI.

items.title: Thought for the week: Companies face cyber pain as hackers press AI advantage
items.summary: IAPP commentary arguing that companies are suffering increasing cyber losses as attackers exploit AI capabilities faster than defenders adapt.

items.title: Investment scams with potential victims in at least 50 countries: over 100 servers seized
items.summary: Europol-supported German-led operation against a supplier of fraudulent trading websites seized over 100 servers, searched 17 locations and arrested suspects; losses exceed EUR 4 million across 50+ countries.

items.title: Security teams want to spot unusual AI agent behavior while they’re still defining normal
items.summary: Abnormal AI's 2026 behavioral security report finds 43% of organisations plan to invest most in monitoring AI agents, while nearly half doubt they can establish baselines for normal agent behaviour.

items.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
items.summary: Google DeepMind researchers used a new AI tool to formally verify the security of the Signal protocol, with ambitions to extend formal verification much more broadly.

items.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: Trump said the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, raising insider and espionage risk questions for the chip sector.

items.title: Trump picks Palantir’s LoSapio to head CISA
items.summary: Trump nominated Palantir's Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, which has lacked a Senate-confirmed director throughout his second term; confirmation may face resistance.

items.title: Anthropic's super bug-finding Mythos model is going into Cisco and IBM products
items.summary: Anthropic's bug-finding Mythos model will be embedded into Cisco and IBM enterprise security products, offering its capabilities without exposing the model itself.

items.title: Vanderbilt University hit in BYOD ransomware attack, data theft claimed
items.summary: Vanderbilt University is responding to an attack claimed by the BYOD ransomware gang, which says it encrypted databases and stole student, employee and research data.

items.title: Europe needs Nvidia. It’ll take more than a spy scandal to change that.
items.summary: Politico argues Europe remains dependent on Nvidia for AI compute regardless of the espionage scandal, given the absence of a homegrown alternative.

items.title: SEGA newsletter data breach exposes 2.2 million email addresses
items.summary: SEGA disclosed a breach at third-party newsletter provider ARARA exposing 2.2 million subscriber email addresses, another reminder of marketing vendor risk.

items.title: Microsoft Fixes RCE Bug in Windows Paint After Weeks of Confusion
items.summary: Microsoft has fixed a remote code execution vulnerability in Windows Paint after weeks of unclear patch communication.

items.title: FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust
items.summary: Microsoft's FORGE Lab used agentic tooling to find memory-safety bugs in Rust's core and std libraries, including safe code paths triggering undefined behaviour via misplaced trust in unsafe code.

items.title: AI Security
items.summary: Schneier's conference write-up frames AI security as three distinct disciplines: security of AI, security with AI and security from AI. Useful framing for building an AI security strategy.

items.title: CalPrivacy Board advances rulemaking to update opt-out preference signals requirements
items.summary: California's privacy board advances rulemaking to update requirements for opt-out preference signals. Limited direct impact outside US-facing operations.

items.title: Not a game: Europol and partners target terrorist role-playing online
items.summary: Europol's EU Internet Referral Unit and 16 countries ran a referral action day against violent extremist and terrorist role-playing in online gaming environments.

items.title: Khor Mor drone attack raises fears over Iraq’s energy security
items.summary: A drone strike on the Khor Mor gas field disrupted electricity supply in Iraqi Kurdistan, renewing concerns over energy infrastructure security and armed group activity.

items.title: Moscow summit tests Russia’s waning grip on former Soviet allies
items.summary: Analysis of the Moscow CSTO summit and Russia's declining influence over former Soviet states as Armenia and others diversify partnerships.

items.title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
items.summary: Blog note on how Claude Fable 5.2 changes code refactoring behaviour depending on how prompts describe code ownership. Relevant for teams standardising AI coding agent prompts.

items.title: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
items.summary: Trump says further US strikes on Iran are 'highly unlikely' while maintaining a 'locked and loaded' posture. Context for regional tensions and related cyber activity.

items.title: European diplomats press Rubio for a role in Russia-Ukraine talks
items.summary: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris as European diplomats press the US for a seat in the Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: US aircraft evacuated from second British base due to Iran threat, WSJ reports
items.summary: US aircraft were reportedly evacuated from a second British base due to Iranian threat, according to WSJ.

items.title: US demands a seat for Europe at Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: US envoys Kushner and Witkoff will press Russia to allow Europe into future negotiations on Ukraine and European security.

items.title: China's trade surplus soars past $1 trillion as AI boom powers exports
items.summary: China's trade surplus surpassed USD 1 trillion as AI-related exports surged, underlining AI's macroeconomic and supply chain weight.

items.title: Taiwan says China is conducting 'area denial' drills in Western Pacific
items.summary: Taiwan says China is running 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific, adding to regional tension.

items.title: Qantas to outsource 850 local jobs with most roles moving to India
items.summary: Qantas will outsource 850 IT jobs, mostly to India, citing modernisation and AI impact. Relevant as a signal on IT outsourcing and third-party risk.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Troubles Leave the AI Industry Reeling
items.summary: WIRED analysis of fallout across the AI industry from the allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy.

items.title: White House nominates Palantir's LoSapio to lead Homeland Security's cyber agency
items.summary: The White House formally nominated Palantir's LoSapio to lead CISA.

items.title: CISA Announces Enhanced Reporting Form for Cyber Incidents
items.summary: CISA launched an enhanced cyber incident reporting form intended to capture richer data for trend analysis and response prioritisation.

items.title: York University breach exposed personal information dating to 2007
items.summary: York University disclosed a breach in which an attacker stole personal data submitted through online forms dating back to 2007.

items.title: Data breach at hearing aid giant Amplifon impacts thousands
items.summary: The US arm of hearing aid maker Amplifon is notifying thousands of customers about a breach earlier this year that exposed medical information.

items.title: Anthropic unveils new Fable, Mythos models as competition heats up ahead of IPO
items.summary: Anthropic released new Fable and Mythos models amid intensifying competition ahead of a planned IPO.

items.title: EU offers cash for Black Sea attack response
items.summary: The EU is offering funding for responses to Black Sea attacks while Washington pursues a diplomatic safe-passage effort with Turkish and Indian proposals.

items.title: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
items.summary: OpenAI describes Control Room, an internal system to track model workloads across its research infrastructure and halt them rapidly on safety or security concerns.

items.title: SignalWire FreeSwitch Code Injection Vulnerability
items.summary: SignalWire FreeSwitch contains a code injection vulnerability that permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution.

items.title: OpenBSD OpenSSH Unexpected Status Code or Return Value Vulnerability
items.summary: OpenBSD OpenSSH on Linux contains an unexpected status code or return value vulnerability that could allow for authentication bypass.

items.title: IBM Aspera Faspex Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
items.summary: IBM Aspera Faspex contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user to craft a specific message to bypass authorization, causing privilege escalations.

items.title: GPUStack Improper Authentication Vulnerability
items.summary: GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml.

items.title: SQL injection in itsourcecode Airline Reservation System
items.summary: itsourcecode Airline Reservation System 1.0 is affected by SQL injection in the flight-management administration endpoint. A remote attacker may alter database operations through the ID input when the affected endpoint is reachable without required privileges.
